Duodenum Histology Analysis

Chloe J McGovern

2025-04-22

Duodenum Histology

Why do you look at the duodenum under the microscope?

It gives us a visual way to see what is happening inside the body. During sample preparation, there can be damage that is done so it is important to note of it is a clinical issue or a methodological limitation.

The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine. In chicks, we find it as a loop with the pancreas in between the two sides. This is important to know because we may see the pancreas depending on how the cross sections are prepared.

When looking under the microscope there are several things we can measure and look for. Starting at the outer most layer (potentially nect to the pancreas) is the mucularis external layer followed by a thick layer of submucosal muscle tissue, followed by a think layer of muscularis mucosae. The top if this later is where the lamina propria begins, and thus the bottom of the crypt depth measurement. This is an important measurement when pared with villi height to determine instestinal homeostasis. It can also be called the invagination site if reading through literature and finding misnomers. The villi are also made of lamina propria and have a more complex physiology but that is for a later time. What matters in this analysis is the villi height, width (taken three times and averaged) and we will alcualte surface area using the equation for a cylinder.

Staining: What do we use and what do we see?

We used PAS (Periodic Acid Schiff-haematoxylin) staining to highlight the goblet cells. Goblet cells can be pink/magenta for neutral pH’s and dark blue/purple for acidic pH’s. Due to the proximity of the duodenum to the stomach, there tends to be more acidic staining goblet cells most likely because of the acidic nature of the chime leaving the stomach (very acidic). It is important to note that goblet cells themselves are NOT acidic or neutral charged, but rather the mucins they produce are acidic which is where the staining color change happens.

source("Code/colors.R")

Prepare column names ahead of time

mix_histo <- mix_histo %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment,
      levels = c("1", "2", "7", "8", "9"),
      labels = c("No Injection", "Water", "Mix Dose 1", "Mix Dose 2", "Mix Dose 3")
    )
  )

#View(mix_histo)

Analysis

1. Villi Height

Height Plain Graph

# violin plot to see the distribution 

height <- ggplot(mix_histo, aes(x = treatment, y = villis_height, fill = treatment)) +
  # full violin
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  # overlay individual points
  geom_jitter(aes(color = treatment),
              width = 0.1, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  # optional: show median + IQR
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point",
               size = 2, color = "white") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = median_hilow, geom = "errorbar",
               width = 0.1, color = "white") +
  # apply your custom palette
  scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors) +
  # minimal theme + Times New Roman
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    text            = element_text(family = "Times New Roman"),
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Villi Height",
    x     = NULL,
    y     = "Microns (μm)"
  )

height

Height Mixed Model

#model
model_height <- lmer(villis_height ~ treatment + (1|biological_rep), data = mix_histo)
summary(model_height)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: villis_height ~ treatment + (1 | biological_rep)
##    Data: mix_histo
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 3499.3
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -2.6699 -0.5754 -0.0031  0.6444  3.7218 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups         Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  biological_rep (Intercept)  125.3   11.20   
##  Residual                   1357.7   36.85   
## Number of obs: 350, groups:  biological_rep, 7
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                     Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)          204.145      6.107  17.436  33.426  < 2e-16 ***
## treatmentWater         2.903      6.228 339.000   0.466    0.641    
## treatmentMix Dose 1  103.327      6.228 339.000  16.590  < 2e-16 ***
## treatmentMix Dose 2   33.531      6.228 339.000   5.384 1.37e-07 ***
## treatmentMix Dose 3   64.049      6.228 339.000  10.284  < 2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) trtmnW trtMD1 trtMD2
## treatmntWtr -0.510                     
## trtmntMxDs1 -0.510  0.500              
## trtmntMxDs2 -0.510  0.500  0.500       
## trtmntMxDs3 -0.510  0.500  0.500  0.500
#post hoc
post_hoc_height <- emmeans(model_height, pairwise ~ treatment)
summary(post_hoc_height)
## $emmeans
##  treatment    emmean   SE   df lower.CL upper.CL
##  No Injection    204 6.11 17.4      191      217
##  Water           207 6.11 17.4      194      220
##  Mix Dose 1      307 6.11 17.4      295      320
##  Mix Dose 2      238 6.11 17.4      225      251
##  Mix Dose 3      268 6.11 17.4      255      281
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## 
## $contrasts
##  contrast                  estimate   SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  No Injection - Water          -2.9 6.23 339  -0.466  0.9903
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 1   -103.3 6.23 339 -16.590  <.0001
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 2    -33.5 6.23 339  -5.384  <.0001
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 3    -64.0 6.23 339 -10.284  <.0001
##  Water - Mix Dose 1          -100.4 6.23 339 -16.124  <.0001
##  Water - Mix Dose 2           -30.6 6.23 339  -4.918  <.0001
##  Water - Mix Dose 3           -61.1 6.23 339  -9.818  <.0001
##  Mix Dose 1 - Mix Dose 2       69.8 6.23 339  11.206  <.0001
##  Mix Dose 1 - Mix Dose 3       39.3 6.23 339   6.306  <.0001
##  Mix Dose 2 - Mix Dose 3      -30.5 6.23 339  -4.900  <.0001
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 5 estimates
# Extract p-values for the pairwise comparisons
p_height <- as.data.frame(post_hoc_height$contrasts)
p_height
##  contrast                    estimate       SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  No Injection - Water        -2.90286 6.228301 339  -0.466  0.9903
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 1 -103.32700 6.228301 339 -16.590  <.0001

## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 5 estimates
# Filter for significant p-values (adjust the threshold as needed, e.g., p < 0.05)
significant_p_height <- p_height[p_height$p.value < 0.05, ]

3. Villus Surface Area

Calculate Surface Area and Make New Column

# check
nrow(mix_histo)
## [1] 350
# should be 350

colnames(mix_histo)
## [1] "treatment"      "biological_rep" "villis_height"  "villis_width1" 
## [5] "villis_width2"  "villis_width3"  "crypt_depth"    "goblet_count"  
## [9] "width_avg"
# make sure you see "width_avg" and "height" in the names


mix_histo <-
  mix_histo %>%
  mutate(
     radius = width_avg / 2,
    surface_area = 2 * pi * radius^2   # top + bottom
                 + 2 * pi * radius * villis_height  # lateral
  )

#View(mix_histo)

Run Mixed Model on Surface Area

#model
model_SA <- lmer(surface_area ~ treatment + (1|biological_rep), data = mix_histo)
summary(model_SA)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: surface_area ~ treatment + (1 | biological_rep)
##    Data: mix_histo
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 7349.5
## 
## Scaled residuals:

p_SA <- ggplot(mix_histo, aes(x = treatment, y = surface_area, fill = treatment)) +
  # full violin
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7, color = "black") +
  # overlay individual points
  geom_jitter(aes(color = treatment),
              width = 0.1, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  # optional: show median + IQR
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point",
               size = 2, color = "white") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = median_hilow, geom = "errorbar",
               width = 0.1, color = "white") +
  # apply your custom palette
  scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors) +
  # minimal theme + Times New Roman
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    text            = element_text(family = "Times New Roman"),
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "C: Villi Surface Area",
    x     = NULL,
    y     = "Surface Area (μm²)"
  ) +
  # Add p-value annotations with larger and spaced lines
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(
      c("No Injection", "Water"),
      c("No Injection", "Mix Dose 1"),
      c("No Injection", "Mix Dose 2"),
      c("No Injection", "Mix Dose 3"),
      c("Water", "Mix Dose 1"),
      c("Water", "Mix Dose 3"),
      c("Mix Dose 1", "Mix Dose 2"),
      c("Mix Dose 1", "Mix Dose 3")),  # Define treatment pairs
    map_signif_level = TRUE,  # Automatically adds p-values
    size = 1,  # Increase the size of the lines for better visibility
    y_position = c(80000, 82500, 85000, 87500, 90000, 92500, 95000, 97500)  # Adjust this to position lines further apart
  )

  ) +

Linear Mixed Model Goblet

#model
model_goblet <- lmer(goblet_count ~ treatment + (1|biological_rep), data = mix_histo)
summary(model_goblet)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: goblet_count ~ treatment + (1 | biological_rep)
##    Data: mix_histo
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 2849
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -2.4818 -0.7350 -0.0148  0.5608  3.1927 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups         Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  biological_rep (Intercept)   6.686   2.586  
##  Residual                   208.920  14.454  
## Number of obs: 350, groups:  biological_rep, 7
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                     Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)           42.029      1.985  37.108  21.175  < 2e-16 ***
## treatmentWater        -1.257      2.443 339.000  -0.515    0.607    
## treatmentMix Dose 1   21.343      2.443 339.000   8.736  < 2e-16 ***
## treatmentMix Dose 2   16.700      2.443 339.000   6.835 3.81e-11 ***
## treatmentMix Dose 3   37.900      2.443 339.000  15.513  < 2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) trtmnW trtMD1 trtMD2
## treatmntWtr -0.615                     
## trtmntMxDs1 -0.615  0.500              
## trtmntMxDs2 -0.615  0.500  0.500       
## trtmntMxDs3 -0.615  0.500  0.500  0.500
#post hoc
post_hoc_goblet <- emmeans(model_goblet, pairwise ~ treatment)
summary(post_hoc_goblet)
## $emmeans
##  treatment    emmean   SE   df lower.CL upper.CL
##  No Injection   42.0 1.98 37.1     38.0     46.0
##  Water          40.8 1.98 37.1     36.8     44.8
##  Mix Dose 1     63.4 1.98 37.1     59.4     67.4
##  Mix Dose 2     58.7 1.98 37.1     54.7     62.7
##  Mix Dose 3     79.9 1.98 37.1     75.9     83.9
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## 
## $contrasts
##  contrast                  estimate   SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  No Injection - Water          1.26 2.44 339   0.515  0.9859
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 1   -21.34 2.44 339  -8.736  <.0001
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 2   -16.70 2.44 339  -6.835  <.0001
##  No Injection - Mix Dose 3   -37.90 2.44 339 -15.513  <.0001
##  Water - Mix Dose 1          -22.60 2.44 339  -9.250  <.0001
##  Water - Mix Dose 2          -17.96 2.44 339  -7.350  <.0001
##  Water - Mix Dose 3          -39.16 2.44 339 -16.027  <.0001
##  Mix Dose 1 - Mix Dose 2       4.64 2.44 339   1.900  0.3191
##  Mix Dose 1 - Mix Dose 3     -16.56 2.44 339  -6.777  <.0001
##  Mix Dose 2 - Mix Dose 3     -21.20 2.44 339  -8.677  <.0001
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 5 estimates
# Extract p-values for the pairwise comparisons
p_goblet <- as.data.frame(post_hoc_goblet$contrasts)
p_goblet
